newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge union sees full talks next week.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge union sees full talks next week.

text.p: The union representing Falconbridge Ltd's striking Ontario workers said on Thursday full scale talks with the company may resume next week.
Negotiations broke off on August 1 when 1,400 unionized workers walked off the job at Falconbridge's Sudbury, Ontario operations.
"I would expect that something probably will happen by the middle of next week," Rolly Gauthier, local 598 president of the Canadian Auto Workers union, said in a telephone interview on Thursday.
While full scale talks have not resumed, a union subcomittee has been trading proposals on shift scheduling with the company for the past week.
Gauthier said the union will respond to the company's latest proposal today.
"There is some movement. It's still far from being where we want to be, but we're going back at it today," he said.
Falconbridge officials were unavailable for comment.
Falconbridge's Sudbury operations last year produced 45,700 metric tons of nickel, 50,000 metric tons of copper and 1,600 metric tons of cobalt, including custom feed.
